record.context_brief: Common splitting fields in tensor-product collapse
record.original_question: If ind(A tensor_F B) is strictly smaller than ind(A) ind(B), what common splitting fields can the division algebras A and B have?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.3. If ind(A tensor_F B) < ind(A) ind(B), what are the common splitting fields for the F-division algebras A and B?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ and $B$ be finite-dimensional central division algebras over $F$. For a central simple $F$-algebra $C$, denote by $\mathrm{ind}(C)$ its Schur index, i.e., the degree of the central division $F$-algebra Brauer-equivalent to $C$. A field extension $L/F$ is called a splitting field of a central simple $F$-algebra $C$ if $C \otimes_F L$ is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over $L$; a common splitting field of $A$ and $B$ is an extension $L/F$ that splits both $A$ and $B$.

Suppose that 
$$\mathrm{ind}(A \otimes_F B) < \mathrm{ind}(A)\,\mathrm{ind}(B).$$
Characterize, as completely as possible, the field extensions $L/F$ that can arise as common splitting fields of $A$ and $B$ under this hypothesis. In particular, determine what constraints (e.g., on the degree, structure, or existence of subfields of given degree) the strict inequality forces on common splitting fields of $A$ and $B$, generalizing the classical fact that when the tensor product of two quaternion division algebras is not a division algebra, the two algebras share a common quadratic splitting field.
artifact.category_tag: central simple algebras and Brauer group
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing common splitting fields of two central division algebras whose tensor product has index strictly less than the product of indices appears to remain open in general. Partial results exist: the classical case of two quaternion algebras (where a common quadratic splitting field exists) is known, and recent work (e.g., Florence; Chapman and others on symbol algebras; the 2013 paper "Tensor products of division algebras and fields") provides further partial results in special cases such as symbol algebras and certain prime-degree settings, but no complete characterization is reported.

status_evidence.title: Common Splitting Fields of Symbol Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies common splitting fields of symbol algebras, generalizing the quaternion case.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area with only partial results for symbol algebras.

status_evidence.title: Tensor Products of Division Algebras and Fields (arXiv:1106.5517)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates when ind(A⊗B) drops below ind(A)ind(B) and related splitting field questions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results, indicating the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Three theorems on common splitting fields of central simple algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Theorems concerning common splitting fields of central simple algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial results, no complete characterization.
